name: ha--night-air-clean-toggle
description: The night air-clean branch forces the unit into fan_only at the room's boost fan speed for the whole air-clean window, unconditionally. Its condition is `{{ night_air_clean_window and (state != 'fan_only' or fan_mode != '5') }}` - no season gate, no allow_night_cooling gate, no enable toggle of any kind. LivingR and BedroomB both run it 03:00-06:00; BedroomS too. Reported 2026-09-23: the owner is woken by BedroomB blowing hard in the middle of the night and wants nothing running there at night at all. Live history confirms the mechanism and rules out the away/return-boost path: on 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 the unit sat at `fan_only | temperature 30 | fan 5` from 03:00 to 06:00 with bedroomb_was_away off and bedroomb_fan_boost_active off throughout, i.e. not cooling - target parked at 30 - but blowing at speed 5 over a sleeping person. No helper value can switch the window off: when air_clean_start equals air_clean_end the window formula falls into its wrap branch `(now >= start or now < end)`, which is always true, so equal times make air-clean run permanently rather than never.

changes: New helper per room: input_boolean.<room>_allow_night_air_clean, exposed as a checkbox on that room's dashboard Tune view because the owner asked for it as a dashboard checkbox, not a code constant
Initial state: bedroomb off (the reported complaint), livingr and bedrooms on, which reproduces today's behaviour for the two rooms nobody complained about

The gate is applied to the night_air_clean_window VARIABLE, not to the air-clean branch. Gating the branch would leave `not night_air_clean_window` false in branches 1 and 6, so anything already running at 02:59 would be stuck until 06:00. Gating the variable makes 03:00-06:00 an ordinary part of the sleep window, which parks the unit off - that is what 'nothing at night' means

The set-line is byte-identical across all three rooms and occurs 97 times in main.tf (livingr 30, bedroomb 35, bedrooms 32). Every edit is scoped to one room's resource block, per the hazard eval 014 documented when it backported a byte-identical predicate
